title: 1st Truth A Summary Of The Proofs Of Createdness And Contingency

questions.question: What are the two main ideas in this passage?
questions.answer: Createdness and contingency.

questions.question: Who studied these two ideas and gave many proofs for them?
questions.answer: Muslim scholars of religion and wise Muslim thinkers.

questions.question: What do people see in the world that shows it does not stay the same?
questions.answer: Change.

questions.question: If the world changes, what does the passage say about the world?
questions.answer: It is not everlasting and it was made.

questions.question: If something was made, what must also be true?
questions.answer: A maker made it.

questions.question: What does it mean if a thing could either exist or not exist?
questions.answer: It is not necessary by itself.

questions.question: What kind of thing cannot be eternal on its own?
questions.answer: A thing that has no reason in itself for being here.

questions.question: Why do scholars use change as a proof?
questions.answer: Because changing things show they began and are not forever by themselves.

questions.question: What is the main lesson this passage teaches about the world?
questions.answer: The world was created by a Maker.

questions.question: What does this passage help a believer understand about Allah’s creation?
questions.answer: Everything in the world depends on Him.

questions.question: What truth comes first in this passage?
questions.answer: The first truth about being created and being contingent.

questions.question: What happens in the world that people can notice?
questions.answer: Things change and move from one state to another.

questions.question: When something changes, what does that tell us about it?
questions.answer: It is not unmade or eternal by itself.

questions.question: What does the passage say must exist if the world was brought into being?
questions.answer: A Creator.

questions.question: Does the passage teach that the world made itself, or that it was made?
questions.answer: It was made.

questions.question: If a thing has no reason in itself to exist rather than not exist, what is it called in meaning?
questions.answer: Possible, not necessary.

questions.question: Why can such a thing not be everlasting by itself?
questions.answer: Because it depends on something else.

questions.question: What are scholars trying to prove with these ideas?
questions.answer: That creation needs a Maker.

questions.question: What did Muslim scholars and sages establish with many proofs?
questions.answer: The truths of createdness and contingency.

questions.question: What do the words about change in the world help us understand?
questions.answer: That the world is not fixed forever on its own.

questions.question: What does “createdness” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: That things were brought into being.

questions.question: What does “contingency” mean here in a simple way?
questions.answer: A thing does not have to exist by itself.

questions.question: If the world is created, what follows next?
questions.answer: It has a Creator.

questions.question: If a thing could either be or not be, is it necessary by itself or not?
questions.answer: Not necessary by itself.

questions.question: What kind of being would be necessary and eternal: one that depends on another, or one that does not?
questions.answer: One that does not depend on another.

questions.question: How does the passage connect change to being created?
questions.answer: Changing shows something is not eternal on its own.

questions.question: How does the passage connect being created to a maker?
questions.answer: If something is made, someone made it.

questions.question: What is the passage mostly trying to explain?
questions.answer: Why the world must be created and need a Maker.

questions.question: Which people are mentioned as teaching these ideas with proofs?
questions.answer: Scholars of religion and Muslim sages.

questions.question: What can we observe in the world every day?
questions.answer: Things change.

questions.question: Why does change matter in this passage?
questions.answer: It shows the world is not eternal by itself.

questions.question: What word fits something that does not last forever?
questions.answer: Temporary.

questions.question: If the world is temporary and made, who must have brought it into being?
questions.answer: A Maker.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a thing that has no built-in reason to exist?
questions.answer: Its existence is only possible, not necessary.

questions.question: Can a merely possible thing be forever on its own, according to the passage?
questions.answer: No, it cannot.

questions.question: What is one cause-and-effect idea in this passage?
questions.answer: Because the world changes, it must be created.

questions.question: Name the two truths talked about at the start of the passage.
questions.answer: Createdness and contingency.

questions.question: What group in Islam is said to have given many proofs for these truths?
questions.answer: Learned Muslim scholars.

questions.question: What sign in the world do they point to first?
questions.answer: Things do not stay the same.

questions.question: If something does not stay the same, what does that say about it?
questions.answer: It began and is not everlasting by itself.

questions.question: What must there be if something began?
questions.answer: One who made it begin.

questions.question: What does it mean when being there and not being there are both possible for a thing?
questions.answer: The thing is not necessary on its own.

questions.question: Why is that important for understanding the world?
questions.answer: It shows the world depends on a Creator.

questions.question: What is the first truth called in this passage?
questions.answer: The truth of createdness and contingency.

questions.question: Who are said to agree on these truths?
questions.answer: Scholars of theology and wise Muslims.

questions.question: What do they notice about the world and everything in it?
questions.answer: It keeps changing.

questions.question: What does that tell them about the world?
questions.answer: It was created and is not eternal by itself.

questions.question: What must exist if the world was created?
questions.answer: A Creator.

questions.question: What is missing inside a contingent thing, according to the passage?
questions.answer: A reason in itself that makes its existence necessary.

questions.question: If a thing lacks that inner necessity, can it be everlasting by itself?
questions.answer: No, it cannot.

questions.question: How do the ideas in the passage fit together?
questions.answer: Change shows createdness, and createdness shows a Creator.
